as_told.title: Shape-recovering foil debris at the crash site

plain: In 1996, after a craft is said to have crashed near Varginha, Brazil, a witness says he picked up a piece of it that sprang back into shape when he bent it. That witness, Carlos de Souza, tells it himself: "this foil or this sheet regained its shape." Jesse Michels interviewed him and repeats the story in other episodes. He describes the material as light and like tinfoil, and says it went back to its original form like a memory metal. He likens it to the debris from Roswell, the 1947 crash in New Mexico at the center of American UFO lore. Italo Venturelli, another guest in the same episode about the case, also mentions the testimony of the man who saw the craft and picked up a piece, though he does not mention the shape-returning. If true, it would mean two crashes decades apart left behind the same strange material.
